h1:
Breakfast Like a Krabi Local
Khanom Jeen, Khao Yam, Dim Sum, Kopi Coffee
intro: People in Krabi get up early to eat, and breakfast here is the best meal of the day because it brings three cultures together on one table — southern-style crab khanom jeen, steaming Hokkien-Chinese dim sum, and khao yam and roti from the Muslim community, all finished off with old-style kopi coffee brewed through a cloth bag. This is a real local's guide to eating breakfast in Krabi, pulled from reviews and from spots that are actually open right now, not places we sat down at ourselves. We've laid out the neighborhood, opening hours, and rough prices so you're ready to go.

blocks.html: Sleep in late in Krabi and you'll miss the meal locals are proudest of. The best breakfast spots start selling at 6 a.m. and plenty of them sell out before noon. Krabi's breakfast has roots in three cultures that have lived side by side for generations: the Hokkien Chinese who make dim sum and old-style coffee, the southern Thais who make khanom jeen with curry sauces and khao yam, and the Muslim community who make roti and budu-dressed khao yam. We've split this guide by what you're eating, then pulled the best spots together into a ranked list.

blocks.text: Crab Khanom Jeen — The Star of a Krabi Breakfast

blocks.html: Khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles) is what people in Krabi eat for breakfast most often. The local signature is nam ya pu — a crab curry sauce made with real crab claw meat, rich and southern-spicy, eaten with a full plate of fresh raw vegetables: yardlong beans, pennywort, cashew shoots, and pickled greens. Some shops offer several sauces — fish curry, fermented-fish (tai pla) curry, green curry, and chili dips. A plate usually runs around 35–50 THB, with all the raw veg you can pile on.

items: Khanom Jeen Kojoi (Krabi town branch) — Krabi's first khanom-jeen-and-fried-chicken shop. Crab curry khanom jeen is about 35 THB a plate, fried chicken about 25 THB a piece. On Maharat Road (town branch closed Mondays; Nuea Khlong branch opens early at 6 a.m.).

Mae Daeng Fresh Noodle Khanom Jeen — Their own freshly made noodles, with several sauces to choose from: crab, barracuda fish, tai pla curry, and jungle curry. Served with a generous spread of raw veg.
Ban Khanom Jeen Ja Lia — A southern khanom jeen shop locals treat as their regular. Rich curry sauces and fresh raw veg.

blocks.text: Steaming Dim Sum — The Town's Hokkien-Chinese Heritage

blocks.html: Krabi has an old Chinese community like Phuket and Trang, so dim sum is a deeply rooted breakfast here. The best shops open at 6 a.m. and serve steaming hot bamboo baskets all morning — har gow, shumai, bao buns, fish balls, and fried bites. A basket runs around 18–25 THB, and some shops have over a hundred items. Locals like to pair it with old-style coffee or hot tea to cut the richness.

blocks.text: Southern Khao Yam + Roti — The Muslim Side of Breakfast

blocks.html: The other half of a Krabi breakfast comes from the Muslim community. Khao yam is steamed rice tossed with finely sliced herbs and a mix of vegetables — lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, toasted coconut, dried shrimp — dressed with a well-balanced budu sauce. It's a light but fully flavored breakfast. Roti, meanwhile, is eaten with chicken curry or condensed milk, found at Islamic eateries that open before dawn. Plates run 20–60 THB.

items: Roti Bang Nara Na Krabi — An Islamic eatery that opens early, around 6:30 a.m., with both khao yam and roti with curry. About 20–60 THB.
Khao yam at Maharat fresh market — The snack and breakfast stalls in the market have khao yam with all the fixings to choose from — good to eat before you walk the market.
Tea and roti at kopi shops — Many old-style coffee shops also sell roti and local sweets alongside the coffee.

blocks.text: 10 Breakfast Spots Krabi Locals Actually Go To

blocks.html: Ordered by popularity, how long they've been around, and consistent reviews — not a definitive ruling on who's tastier, since each shop is strong at something different. Prices and hours are rough estimates; double-check with the shop before you go.

items.name: Yuan Bao
items.blurb: A big dim sum shop that locals and visitors alike rank near the top, with over a hundred dim sum items — crab shumai, har gow, bao buns — plus khanom jeen, khao yam, and various soups all in one place. The space is roomy and comfortable, good for families and solo diners alike.
items.meta: Open ~6:30 a.m.–3 p.m. daily · Krabi town

items.name: Khanom Jeen Kojoi
items.blurb: Krabi's first khanom-jeen-and-fried-chicken shop. The crab curry sauce uses real crab meat, eaten with fried chicken that's crisp outside and tender inside plus a full plate of raw veg. It's the name people in Krabi think of first when khanom jeen comes up.
items.meta: Town branch at 32 Maharat Rd (closed Mondays) · Nuea Khlong branch open ~6 a.m.–7 p.m.
items.price: Crab curry khanom jeen ~35 THB · fried chicken ~25 THB/piece

items.name: Sai Mai Dim Sum
items.blurb: An old-school dim sum shop going on nearly 30 years, in the morning-market area right on Maharat Road. It's the image of traditional Chinese-Krabi breakfast. The bestsellers are pork shumai and seaweed-wrapped pork, with fresh hot baskets coming out all morning.
items.meta: Open ~6–11 a.m. · Maharat Rd, morning-market area
items.price: Tens of baht per basket · ~60–120 THB per person

items.name: Ratcharot Dim Sum
items.blurb: Cantonese-style dim sum steamed fresh every day, with several single-plate breakfast dishes to add on. The atmosphere is easygoing — good for anyone who wants a full dim sum spread without queueing at the busiest shop in town.

items.name: Pae Yim Dim Sum (by Lee)
items.blurb: A well-known dim sum shop on Maharat Road. The standouts are Phuket fish balls, fish-filled tofu, and har gow, about 20 THB a basket. Open from 6 a.m. — good for dim sum fans who want that southern sea-fish flavor.

items.name: Mae Daeng Fresh Noodle Khanom Jeen
items.blurb: Khanom jeen with house-made fresh noodles. The draw is the range of sauces — crab curry with claw meat, barracuda fish curry, tai pla curry, jungle curry, and chili dip — eaten with all the fresh raw veg you want.

items.name: Dim Sum Soi 14
items.blurb: A dim sum shop in a residential area on Krabi Road, Soi 14, with steamed baskets and fried bites plus single-plate breakfasts. Open from 6 a.m., it's where people in the neighborhood stop in before work.

items.name: Krabi Dim Sum
items.blurb: A dim sum shop open from morning to noon, across from Krabi Hospital — good for late risers who want dim sum but miss the shops that close early. A full menu of both steamed and fried.
items.meta: Open ~6 a.m.–12 p.m. · across from Krabi Hospital

items.name: Roti Bang Nara Na Krabi
items.blurb: An Islamic eatery open before dawn, serving southern khao yam with all the sides plus roti with chicken curry or condensed milk. It's the Muslim side of Krabi breakfast that a lot of people overlook, at friendly prices.

items.name: Sueng Kopi Dim Sum (Ao Nang)
items.blurb: A breakfast spot on the Ao Nang side that brings old-style kopi coffee, dim sum, and breakfast bites together in one place. Good for anyone staying near the beach who doesn't want to drive into town for breakfast — coffee and dim sum in a single meal.
items.price: Drinks + dim sum, tens to low hundreds of baht

blocks.title: How to Catch the Good Stuff at Breakfast
blocks.html: The old-school khanom jeen and dim sum shops like Sai Mai and Pae Yim sell out fast, so if you want everything, get there before 8 a.m. Late risers should pick Yuan Bao or Krabi Dim Sum, which stay open till noon. Staying around Ao Nang? Stop at a kopi shop near the beach first — no need to drive into town.

blocks.text: "Kopi" Old-Style Coffee, the Krabi Breakfast Pairing

blocks.html: The word kopi comes from Malay and means coffee — it's the traditional coffee-shop culture you'll find across southern Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore. The coffee is dark-roasted, brewed through a cloth bag, and mixed with sweetened condensed milk, with a heavy flavor that cuts the richness of dim sum and fried food well. At Ban Ra-mad on Koh Klang, there's still a community that roasts, pounds, and brews kopi by hand the traditional way, selling it for just a few baht a glass — a coffee heritage that's getting harder to find every year.

items: Hot kopi — dark-roasted black coffee with sweetened condensed milk, bold and the best match for dim sum.
Oliang — iced black coffee with sugar, refreshing in the southern heat.
Hot tea / black tea — for non-coffee drinkers; cuts the richness of fried food well.
Kopi at Ban Ra-mad (Koh Klang) — hand-made kopi from the Muslim community; take a boat across from the town pier. Just a few baht a glass.

blocks.text: Morning Market — Start Breakfast at Maharat Fresh Market

blocks.html: If you want to see a Krabi breakfast with everything in one place, head to Maharat Fresh Market in the center of town. It's a morning market that's busy before sunrise, with fresh produce, seafood, vegetables, fruit, and breakfast stalls — khanom jeen, khao yam, and local sweets like khanom chan, khanom piakpoon, bachang, and sticky rice in banana leaf. Graze your way through and you'll try plenty for just a couple hundred baht.

items.name: Maharat Fresh Market
items.blurb: Krabi's central morning market, right on Maharat Road, open roughly 4 a.m.–12 p.m. A full spread of breakfast: khanom jeen, khao yam, local sweets.

items.name: Local Sweets in the Market
items.blurb: Khanom chan, khanom piakpoon, bachang, sticky rice in banana leaf, kalamae — southern desserts that go well with old-style coffee.

items.name: Fresh Southern Raw Veg
items.blurb: The market has the fresh raw vegetables khanom jeen shops use — cashew shoots, pennywort, yardlong beans.

items.name: Krabi Walking Street
items.blurb: Near Maharat Market, open Friday–Sunday evenings if you want street food for a later meal.

blocks.title: Straight Talk
blocks.html: A lot of breakfast spots in Krabi are traditional local shops — tables can be packed at rush hour, parking is tight, and some places are mostly cash. Bring cash and make peace with the queues on long weekends. Khao yam and crab curry sauce here are spicier than in central Thailand, so if you don't eat spicy, ask the cook to dial it down. But that heat is exactly the charm of eating breakfast like a Krabi local.

faq.q: What Krabi breakfast dishes should I try?
faq.a: The three main ones are southern-style crab khanom jeen, steaming Hokkien-Chinese dim sum, and khao yam with roti from the Muslim community — finished off with old-style kopi coffee brewed through a cloth bag. It's a breakfast that brings the town's three cultures together.

faq.q: Which Krabi dim sum shop is famous, and what time does it open?
faq.a: Yuan Bao is the big shop locals rank near the top, open around 6:30 a.m.–3 p.m. with over a hundred items. Sai Mai and Pae Yim are the old-timers on Maharat Road that open at 6 a.m. and sell out fast — go before 8 a.m. if you want the full spread.

faq.q: Where's the best crab khanom jeen in Krabi?
faq.a: Khanom Jeen Kojoi is Krabi's first khanom-jeen-and-fried-chicken shop, with crab curry sauce made from real crab meat at around 35 THB a plate; the town branch is on Maharat Road. Mae Daeng Fresh Noodle Khanom Jeen stands out for its range of sauces and house-made fresh noodles.

faq.q: How is Krabi's old-style kopi coffee different from regular coffee?
faq.a: Kopi is dark-roasted coffee brewed through a cloth bag with sweetened condensed milk — heavier than typical fresh coffee. It's a traditional Malay-Chinese coffee-shop culture. At Ban Ra-mad on Koh Klang, a community still roasts and brews it by hand the old way, selling it for just a few baht a glass.

faq.q: Where is Krabi's morning market and what time does it open?
faq.a: Maharat Fresh Market is in the center of town right on Maharat Road, open roughly 4 a.m.–12 p.m. It has a full breakfast spread — khanom jeen, khao yam, and local sweets like khanom chan and bachang — perfect for grazing before you start sightseeing.
